The strongest ground is that the promise was oral, since most states require a signed writing to revive a debt the statute of limitations has barred. Lack of consideration is weaker, because a promise to pay a time-barred debt is generally binding without new consideration (Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82), and the "deadbeat" remark neither supplies consideration nor creates duress. The team note overstates the point: limitations usually bars the remedy rather than extinguishing the debt, so the oral promise fails on the writing requirement, not because the debt no longer exists.

CONFIDENCE: 62
